lines: - Analyze a closure literal passed directly to `Closure::bind()`, or used as the receiver of `->bindTo()` or `->call()`, in the scope it is bound to when that scope is a known class (`Foo::class`, `'Foo'`, or an object of a single known class), as if it had `@phan-closure-scope Foo`: accesses to private and protected members of the bound class and `$this`, `self::` and `static::` inside the closure no longer produce false positives such as `PhanAccessClassConstantPrivate`. `$this` stays undefined when the closure is bound to `null`, and nothing is inferred when the bound object is not an instance of the scope class. A closure stored in a variable before being bound still needs the annotation ([#5260](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5260))

- `--phase-timings-json` and `--dump-phase-timings` record PHP's cycle collector statistics for the main process and each analysis worker: `gc_enabled`, `gc_runs`, `gc_collected`, `gc_roots` and, on PHP 8.3+, `gc_collector_s`

- `PHPUnitNotDeadCodePlugin` recognizes the attributes of PHPUnit 10+: methods with `#[Test]`, the data providers named by `#[DataProvider]` and `#[DataProviderExternal]`, and the hook methods with `#[Before]`, `#[After]`, `#[BeforeClass]`, `#[AfterClass]`, `#[PreCondition]` or `#[PostCondition]` (or the corresponding `@before`, `@after`, ... annotations) are marked as referenced for `--dead-code-detection`, like the methods starting with `test`, `@test` methods and `@dataProvider` methods already were. All `@dataProvider` annotations of a test are now followed instead of only the first, and the attributes and annotations of tests, data providers and hook methods that a trait provides to the test case are now seen (also when the test case renames the method or changes its visibility, and `self::class` in a `#[DataProviderExternal]` of a trait is the class using the trait) ([#5629](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5629))

+- `@inheritDoc` on a constructor now inherits the phpdoc types of the constructor of the parent class: a parameter without a type of its own gets the type of the parent constructor's parameter of the same name, and so does the property it promotes (also as its declared type, for the checks of assignments to the property). A parameter documented with the inline `@var` of its promoted property keeps that type. A constructor does not have to be compatible with the constructor of the parent class, so its types are inherited by name and only with the annotation, where the other methods inherit their missing types by position by default (`inherit_phpdoc_types`). A constructor implementing an abstract constructor already inherited the types of its parameters by position; the properties it promotes now get those types too. The template types of a generic class inherited this way (`@template U` with `@extends P<U>`) are used to infer the type of `new C(...)` ([#5631](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5631))

+- `PhanCommentInheritDocOnNonOverrideMethod` is now also emitted for `@inheritDoc` on a constructor when no ancestor declares a constructor: the constructor is no longer exempt from the check as a magic method ([#5631](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5631))

- Configure the internal functions and the methods of internal classes that plugins know about (return type overrides, function call analyzers) when the analyzed code first uses them, instead of loading all of them at the start of the analysis phase. The built-in plugins mention about 200 functions and the `Closure`, `ReflectionClass` and `ReflectionFunction` classes, and most runs call few of them. Plugins can use `CodeBase::whenFunctionIsLoaded()` and `CodeBase::whenInternalClassIsLoaded()` for the same purpose. The new `HandleLazyLoadInternalMethodCapability` is the counterpart of `HandleLazyLoadInternalFunctionCapability` for the methods of internal classes loaded during the analysis phase: `CallableParamPlugin` uses it to check the callable and class-string parameters of those methods (e.g. `Closure::fromCallable()`), which previously had no checks when the class was loaded during analysis ([#5626](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5626))

- Fix false positive `PhanUnreferencedClass` with `--dead-code-detection` and `PHPUnitNotDeadCodePlugin` for every test case class: the reference the plugin added to the class was ignored as a reference from within the class itself ([#5629](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5629))

- Fix false positive `PhanWriteOnlyPrivateProperty`, `PhanReadOnlyPrivateProperty`, `PhanUnreferencedPrivateProperty`, `PhanUnreferencedPrivateMethod` and `PhanUnreferencedPrivateClassConstant` with `--dead-code-detection` for a property, method or constant (PHP 8.2+) that a class declares with the same name as a property, an abstract or concrete method, a `@method` or a constant of a trait it uses: `$this->prop`, `$this->method()` and `self::X` in the trait now count as references to the class's declaration, as they already did for a `@property` of the trait. Uses of the class's property or constant also count as references to the trait's declaration of the same name, as they do when the class does not redeclare it, so a trait property that is only written through the class's declaration is no longer reported as `PhanReadOnlyPrivateTraitProperty`. This also applies to traits used through other traits ([#5630](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5630))

+- Fix the template types of a method overriding a method of a generic interface in a class that also has a parent class: they were mapped with the `@extends` annotation of the parent class instead of the `@implements` annotation of the interface (`@implements I<int>` on the class, or `@implements I<T>` on a parent class with `@extends P<int>` on the class), which left the template type unbound in the signature checks (a false positive `PhanParamSignatureMismatch` for an override with `@param int`) and in the phpdoc types inherited with `inherit_phpdoc_types`. The `@extends` and `@implements` annotations are now followed through the parent classes and interfaces of the class ([#5631](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5631))

- Fix false positive `PhanUnreferencedProtectedMethod` and `PhanUnreferencedPrivateTraitMethod` with `--dead-code-detection` for a protected or private method of a trait used through another trait, depending on the order of the declarations: the copy of the method in the class using the outer trait now refers to the inner trait's declaration, as the copies of properties and constants already did ([#5632](https://github.com/phan/phan/pull/5632))

- Emit `PhanPossiblyUndeclaredVariable` (and `PhanPossiblyUndeclaredGlobalVariable`) for reads of an element of a possibly undeclared variable, such as `echo $var[0]`, `$x = $var['k'][1]`, `foreach ($var[0] as ...)`, `$var[0]++`, `$var[0] .= 'a'` or `f($var[0])` when the parameter is not by reference, as already happened for `$var` and `$var->prop`. Writes (`$var[0] = 1`, `$var[0] ??= 1`, `unset($var[0])`), references (`$x = &$var[0]`, `sort($var[0])`) and `isset`, `empty` and `??` are not reported ([#5621](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5621))

- Fix false positive `PhanUnreferencedPrivateClassConstant`/`PhanUnreferencedProtectedClassConstant` with `--dead-code-detection` for a private or protected constant declared in a trait and used from a class using the trait: uses of the class's copy now count as references to the trait's constant, as they already did for trait properties and methods. A trait constant that is really unused is now reported once, on the trait, instead of once on the trait and once more for every class using it ([#5619](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5619))
